title: enforce-release-lock-and-backup-verifier-for-tenant-rollback-scenarios
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We've seen two incidents where a failed or partial upgrade left tenant state inconsistent and allowed a subsequent downgrade to silently corrupt data. This PR adds coordinated release locks, a pre-upgrade backup/verifier step, and a tenant-aware rollback sequencer to reduce blast radius and make rollbacks safe. High level: 1) A 'release-lock' resource is created in Terraform that gates concurrent upgrades per-cluster and per-tenant; upgrades will fail fast if a lock exists. 2) Installer CLI gains 'installer verify-backup --tenant <id>' which performs a lightweight restore dry-run against a minimal scratch namespace (K8s) validating snapshot integrity and schema compatibility. 3) Helm chart value validation now performs a downgrade-guard check (prevents applying charts with lower appVersion or incompatible CRD schema). 4) Operator hooks include a rollback-sequencer which requires a previously verified snapshot to proceed, and will refuse rollbacks if volume snapshots are missing or checksum mismatches occur. 5) Terraform remote state workflows are updated: when an upgrade starts we write a short-lived 'upgrade-token' into the remote state that is used by other automation to detect in-flight upgrades; the token is removed on success/failure. Migration flow: preflight -> verify-backup -> create-release-lock -> run migration -> remove-release-lock or leave for manual reconciliation on failure. Safety considerations: - All checks are opt-out via installer flags for air-gapped/private installs where snapshotting is managed externally. - The default behavior in the next release is opt-in behind a feature-flag; we ran this PR behind feature=rollback_safety during dogfood runs. Implementation details and files changed: see changed_files. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for Terraform plan changes and Helm value checks. - Integration e2e using a local-kind cluster + minio snapshots to run verify-backup flow. - Simulated downgrade attempts added to canary tests to assert the helm-downgrade-guard blocks the change. Rollout plan: 1) Release as a behind-flag feature, 2) enable for internal-managed private clusters, 3) enable by default after 2 weeks of telemetry. Backwards compatibility: existing private installs are unaffected unless operator-level feature flag is flipped on. Related: ENG-8473 (upgrade-rollback-playbook), SUP-1198 (customer incident for partial rollback). Checklist: - [x] Terraform release-lock resource and docs - [x] CLI verify-backup command + tests - [x] Helm downgrade guard and schema validator - [x] Operator rollback-sequencer + unit/integration tests - [x] E2E smoke tests against local environment - [x] Release notes and runbook updated

review_thread: Arjun Patel (reviewer): Can we avoid creating an extra dependency on the remote state provider for customers who manage state externally? Suggest making release-token optional and fall back to a CRD-based lock.

Maya Chen (author): Good point. Implemented an optional CRD lock fallback and exposed terraform var 'use_remote_state_lock' (default true). Updated docs to show disabling remote token and using CRD lock instead.

Sofia Martínez (reviewer): Helm chart change looks good, but validate-values-hook may block legitimate operator-driven CRD upgrades. Please add an escape hatch and document how to approve a migration that requires CRD schema bump.
Maya Chen (author): Added '--force-crd-upgrade' flag for operator controller and a required annotation 'redwood.io/force-crd-upgrade=true' to opt-in; documented in charts README.
Noah Kim (reviewer, approve): Verified e2e run on internal cluster; CI flake (lint) was fixed in commit c1f0a2b. Approving.
Arjun Patel (maintainer, approve): Looks safe; small nit about log verbosity which was addressed. Approving and squashing on merge.
ci_checks: lint: pass (was failing on first run; fixed in c1f0a2b)
merge: merged via squash (maintainer: Arjun Patel). Merge commit message: 'enforce release locks + backup verifier for safer rollbacks (ENG-8473)'.
release_notes: Private installer: add optional release-locking and pre-upgrade backup verification to reduce rollback risk. New CLI command 'installer verify-backup'. Helm charts now block downgrades by default behind the 'rollback_safety' feature flag. See docs/runbooks/upgrade-rollback-safety.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: If enabling rollback_safety in production, ensure snapshot retention policy is at least 7 days and configure your object-storage credentials for the verify-backup dry-run. For Terraform users who disable remote-state locks, enable the CRD fallback before performing concurrent upgrades.
testing_summary: Local kind+minio integration ran 3/3 passing scenarios: preflight success, verified snapshot dry-run, prevented downgrade attempt. Load test: 50 concurrent upgrade requests show release_lock prevents parallel runs; no data corruption observed.
follow_up: Plan a telemetry event in 2 weeks to observe failure rates and any manual overrides. Consider exposing laddered grace periods for the release-lock token on next iteration.
